description: baseline

Implement a CUTE DSL tiled unblocked Householder path for small n=32,176,352 using one CTA per matrix with warp-level reductions and in-place H and tau output, keeping torch.geqrf fallback for n>=512 to reduce geomean tail without risking large-shape correctness.
Prototype CUTE DSL copy/identity path for n=32 built but validation raised a CuTe MLIR exception under the multiprocessing checker.
Added a CUTE DSL serial unblocked Householder path for n=32 with torch.geqrf fallback for larger shapes; correctness passes but n=32 is much slower than torch.geqrf.
Tried a warp-parallel CUTE QR32 using warp_redux_sync and sync_warp; build passed but validation raised a CuTe MLIR exception at first n=32 test.

Fixed the CUTE QR32 path by replacing unsupported float redux with shuffle-based warp reductions and preserving diagonal on zero-sigma columns; n=32 improves strongly while larger shapes still use torch.geqrf.
Tried to generalize the warp CUTE QR kernel to n=32/176/352, but direct small-shape probing segfaulted after import/build.
Tried a specialized CUTE QR176 column-parallel kernel; it compiled but direct probes failed QR residual checks and also destabilized the QR32 result in-process.

Best valid result is c8dccb5245d587a9266b24d48b91e952f5e03947 at linalg/qr_v2=97600.112 us vs baseline 115824.174 us (~1.19x geomean speedup). The useful change is a CUTE DSL one-CTA/one-warp QR32 Householder kernel using shuffle-based warp reductions; serial QR32 was slower, warp_redux_sync emitted unsupported redux.f32 for sm_120a, and attempts to extend this design to n=176/352 either segfaulted or failed residual checks. Suggested next brief: either independently specialize n=176 with multiple CTAs/warps and shared-memory panel state, or keep c8dccb52 as a safe QR32-only improvement and optimize fallback overhead/noise.

Starting from the valid CUTE QR32 branch, implement an independent CUTE DSL n=176 specialization using multi-warp panel reductions and shared-memory column state rather than generalizing QR32 code; keep QR32 unchanged and fallback to torch.geqrf unless n=176 residual and orthogonality checks pass.
Added independent CUTE DSL n=176 Householder specialization with 256-thread multi-warp reductions and QR32 unchanged; validation passes and geomean improves, with n=176 at ~6509 us.
Tried reducing QR176 to 128 threads/four warps; correctness still passes but n=176 slows to ~7864 us and geomean regresses.
Restored the faster 256-thread/eight-warp CUTE QR176 path after 128-thread variant regressed; keeping prior validated metric for this code state.
Cached the active QR176 Householder column in shared memory while leaving QR32 unchanged; validation and guards pass, n=176 improves to ~5566 us and geomean to 89671.447 us.

Best result is commit 9673e143 with a dedicated CUTE DSL n=176 specialization using 256-thread multi-warp reductions plus shared-memory caching of the active Householder column; full validation and guards passed, benchmark geomean improved to 89671.447 us and n=176 to ~5566 us. A 128-thread/four-warp variant was valid but slower at 92272.608 geomean, so it was abandoned. Final nsys profile was captured for 9673e143; next promising direction is reducing the remaining per-column sync count or mapping each trailing update column group across warps to improve QR176 further.

Replace 964bdcba's n=176 dispatch arm with 9673e143's faster shared-memory-cached n=176 CUTE specialization while preserving 964bdcba's QR32, 4096 upper, and 512 rankdef predicates exactly; keep torch.geqrf fallback for all other cases and benchmark composition.
Combined 964bdcba dispatch predicates with 9673e143 shared-memory-cached CUTE QR176 specialization; preserved QR32, 4096 upper fast path, and 512 rankdef path; validation and guards pass.

Combined parent 964bdcba with 9673e143 by replacing only the n=176 CUTE dispatch arm with the shared-memory-cached QR176 kernel while preserving QR32, 4096 upper, 512 rankdef predicates, and torch.geqrf fallback. Commit dc16dc4d passed build, full validation, differential and invariance guards; benchmark geomean linalg/qr_v2=88007.044 us (better than both parents locally), with n=176 at ~5566 us. Captured nsys profile worker-2-brief-2-iteration-0-dc16dc4d2463a136571d663cca86b77b1b569b8f.nsys-rep. Brief exhausted: requested combine is complete; remaining possible work is outside this combine brief, e.g. new brief for n=352 CUTE specialization or reducing QR176 sync/update cost.

Starting from the best stacked CUTE branch, implement an independent n=352 CUTE Householder specialization using 256 or 512 threads with multi-warp reductions and shared-memory active-column caching; keep QR32, n=176, n=512 structural, and 4096 upper paths unchanged, and fallback unless n=352 residual and orthogonality checks pass.

Added independent 256-thread CUTE n=352 Householder kernel with shared active-column caching; build passed but full validation did not complete within budget because the per-column serial update path was too slow.
Changed n=352 CUTE specialization to 512 threads / 16 warps to reduce row-loop work; build passed but targeted n=352 probe still exceeded practical runtime budget before returning.
Fixed QR352 512-thread warp scratchpad to 16 entries; build passed, but the candidate remained impractical to validate under scheduler pressure and still relies on serial per-column update work.

Replaced monolithic QR352 with a CUTE multi-launch Householder path: copy init, per-column panel kernel, and one CTA per trailing column update. Full validation and guards pass; n=352 benchmark improves to ~30.184 ms and geomean to 83102.293 us.
Retuned multi-launch CUTE QR352 from 512 to 256 threads / 8 warps per CTA. Full validation and guards pass; n=352 improves to ~29.910 ms and geomean to 83006.824 us.
Retuned multi-launch CUTE QR352 update/panel kernels to 128 threads / 4 warps. Full validation and both guards pass; n=352 improves to ~29.415 ms and geomean to 82917.813 us.
Retuned multi-launch CUTE QR352 panel/update kernels to 64 threads / 2 warps. Full validation and both guards pass; n=352 improves to ~29.389 ms and geomean to 82914.546 us.
Tried 32-thread/one-warp QR352 multi-launch kernels, but the broad thread-count edit also altered QR176 shared reduction sizing and benchmark correctness failed on n=176; abandoning this variant.

Kept the 64-thread / 2-warp CUTE QR352 multi-launch specialization but restored QR176 warp scratch sizing to 8 entries. Full validation and guards pass; benchmark geomean is 82889.671 us with n=352 at ~29.404 ms.

Brief exhausted. Best valid result is e8e1f52d0182ecfe3d5625e8588aa3340d89a6dd with an independent CUTE n=352 Householder specialization implemented as multi-launch kernels: copy init, per-column panel/norm/tau, and one CTA per trailing column update. It preserves existing QR32, QR176, n=512 structural, and 4096 upper paths; full validation plus differential and invariance guards pass. Best local benchmark linalg/qr_v2=82889.670920 us, improving n=352 to ~29.404 ms and geomean from parent ~84709.948 us. Captured nsys profile worker-2-brief-3-iteration-8-e8e1f52d0182ecfe3d5625e8588aa3340d89a6dd.nsys-rep. Failed/abandoned attempts: monolithic one-CTA QR352 at 256/512 threads was correct-or-built but too slow to validate; 32-thread sweep accidentally regressed QR176 and failed correctness. Further n=352 gains likely require reducing the 704 per-call launch count via fused panel/update batching or a true tiled trailing-update kernel.

Reduce QR352 launch overhead by fusing each Householder panel kernel with a small batch of trailing-column updates, or batching multiple update columns per launch while preserving the validated 64-thread, 2-warp arithmetic and exact n=352 dispatch; keep existing fast paths unchanged and fallback or revert unless validation passes and n=352 plus geomean improves.

Batched QR352 trailing update kernel to process four columns per CTA while preserving the validated 64-thread/2-warp reduction path. Full validation and guards pass; n=352 improves from ~29.4 ms to ~17.39 ms and geomean to 79291.063 us.

Tried expanding QR352 trailing updates from four to eight columns per CTA, but validation failed at CUTE runtime code generation because the launch wrapper still referenced the removed _qr352_update4_kernel symbol.
Fixed the QR352 eight-column CUTE update launch. Full validation and guards pass; n=352 improves to ~14.065 ms and geomean to 77908.764 us.
Expanded QR352 CUTE update batching to sixteen trailing columns per CTA. Full validation and guards pass; n=352 improves to ~11.655 ms and geomean to 76820.414 us.

Tried QR352 CUTE update batching at thirty-two columns per CTA. Full validation and guards pass, but n=352 regresses to ~12.601 ms and geomean to 77176.403 us versus the sixteen-column variant, likely from register pressure/occupancy loss.
Reverted the slower thirty-two-column QR352 batching attempt, restoring the previously validated sixteen-column update kernel as branch HEAD; same code and metric as iteration 3.

Expanded QR352 CUTE update batching to twenty-four trailing columns per CTA. Full validation and guards pass; n=352 improves to ~11.381 ms and geomean to 76497.031 us, beating sixteen-column and thirty-two-column variants.
Tried QR352 CUTE update batching at twenty-eight columns per CTA. Full validation and guards pass, but n=352 regresses to ~11.760 ms and geomean to 76775.876 us versus the twenty-four-column best.
Reverted the slower twenty-eight-column QR352 batching attempt, restoring the previously validated twenty-four-column update kernel as branch HEAD; same code and metric as iteration 6.

Brief exhausted. Best valid result is bb18ed68cfb81fba4978dcb4c884ed9f3a68ed6d, which restores/keeps the twenty-four-column QR352 CUTE trailing-update batch kernel. It preserves the existing QR32, QR176, 512 structural, 4096 upper, and torch.geqrf fallback paths; full validation plus differential and invariance guards pass. Best local benchmark was linalg/qr_v2=76497.031353 us, with n=352 improved to ~11.381 ms from parent ~29.4 ms; 4, 8, 16, 24 improved progressively, while 28 and 32 regressed. Captured nsys profile worker-2-brief-4-iteration-8-bb18ed68cfb81fba4978dcb4c884ed9f3a68ed6d.nsys-rep. Remaining launch overhead is one panel launch plus one batched update launch per k; next useful brief would fuse panel with first update tile or reduce the 352 panel launches.

Starting from the 24-column QR352 best, reduce remaining QR352 launch overhead by batching two adjacent Householder panel columns per launch or trying intermediate 20- and 22-column update tile sizes between the 16- and 24-column winners; preserve exact n=352 dispatch and revert unless full validation plus n=352 and geomean improve.
